slides.headline: How to use *Otter AI* for meeting notes, free plan explained

slides.heading: 1. Send the *Notetaker* to your call
paras: Otter Notetaker joins Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams as a guest and transcribes live.
Connect Google or Microsoft calendar under Apps and it can join meetings on its own.

slides.heading: 2. Or record *without a bot*
paras: The Mac and Windows desktop app, the Chrome extension and the phone app can record on your own device.
You can also upload audio and video files.

slides.heading: 3. Ask *Otter Chat* about the meeting
paras: Open the Otter Chat tab in the Takeaways panel and ask for key topics, a follow-up email or minutes.
On the free plan you get 3 questions per conversation.

slides.heading: 4. Know the *free limits*
paras: Basic gives 300 minutes a month, 30 minutes per conversation, 3 file imports for life and your 25 most recent conversations.
Pro starts at $8.33 a month billed yearly.

site_article.headline: How to use Otter AI for meeting notes, and what the free plan gets you
site_article.dek: Otter joins your Zoom, Google Meet or Teams calls, writes a live transcript and a summary. Here is how to set it up, how to ask it questions and where the free plan runs out.
site_article.summary: Otter AI is a meeting notetaker that transcribes calls and writes summaries and action items. The free Basic plan includes 300 transcription minutes a month, with a 30 minute limit per conversation.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Otter AI: meeting notes and free plan limits
site_article.seo_description: How to use Otter AI: add the Notetaker to Zoom, Meet or Teams, record without a bot, ask Otter Chat questions, and the exact free plan limits.
site_article.answer_summary: To use Otter AI, sign up at otter.ai, connect your Google or Microsoft calendar under Apps so Otter Notetaker can join your Zoom, Google Meet or Teams calls, or record with the desktop app, Chrome extension or phone app. The free Basic plan gives 300 minutes a month and 30 minutes per conversation.
site_article.hero_alt: Promotional image for Otter, an AI meeting notetaker.

paragraphs.text: How to use Otter AI, in short: sign up, connect your calendar, and let Otter Notetaker join your Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams calls. It writes a live transcript with speaker names, then a summary with decisions and action items. You can also record without a bot through the desktop app, the Chrome extension or the phone app.

There is a free plan. Otter's pricing page lists Basic as free forever, with 300 transcription minutes per user each month and a limit of 30 minutes per conversation. That is enough to try it on a few short calls a week. It is not enough for long meetings.
Getting started with Otter AI

paragraphs.title: 1. Create an account
paragraphs.text: Go to otter.ai and sign up with an email address, a Google account or a Microsoft account. Otter also has apps for iPhone and Android, and a desktop app for Mac and Windows.

paragraphs.title: 2. Connect your calendar
paragraphs.text: In the left menu, click Apps. Scroll to the calendar section and click Add next to Google or Microsoft, then sign in. Your events sync to your Otter homepage, and Notetaker can join any event that has a Zoom, Google Meet or Teams link. Zoom needs an extra setup step that Otter describes in a separate help article.

paragraphs.title: 3. Choose how Notetaker joins
paragraphs.text: All Notetaker settings live under Account Settings, then Meetings. That is where you decide whether it joins your calendar meetings automatically.

Notetaker joins as a guest named after you, for example "Sam's Notetaker". If it cannot get in, the meeting may block guests. Ask the host or your IT team to allow them. Otter itself recommends getting consent from everyone before you record.
Notetaker leaves on its own after 12 minutes of continuous silence, or 5 minutes after the scheduled end if the meeting runs over. It cannot sign in to a Zoom, Meet or Teams account.
How to record without a bot

Some people do not want a bot in the participant list. Otter's homepage lists bot-free recording through the Mac or Windows desktop app and the Chrome extension, recording on iOS and Android, and uploads of audio and video files for transcription.

paragraphs.title: Use the Chrome extension for Google Meet or Zoom
paragraphs.text: Install the Otter extension from the Chrome Web Store with Add to Chrome. Open your meeting link in Chrome, click the extension and choose Add AI Notetaker. For Google Meet you can instead pick Record on my device instead, as long as Otter is not already recording.

The extension has real limits. It works only in Chrome, only with Google Meet and Zoom, and Otter's help page says Microsoft Teams and Webex are not supported. The live floating transcript appears only in Google Meet; Zoom transcripts show up in My Conversations. Supported languages for the extension are English, Spanish and French.
How to use Otter Chat after the meeting
Otter Chat answers questions about one conversation, based only on its transcript. It works during the meeting and after it. Everyone in the conversation can see the questions and answers.

paragraphs.title: 1. Open the chat
paragraphs.text: Open the conversation and click the Otter Chat tab in the Takeaways panel on the right.

paragraphs.title: 2. Ask your question
paragraphs.text: Pick a suggested prompt or type your own, starting with @otter, and press Enter. You can mention other participants with @ to notify them, or reply to a message.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Get the follow-up email
paragraphs.text: @otter Draft a short follow-up email to everyone in this meeting. List the decisions we made and each action item with the person responsible.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Find the open questions
paragraphs.text: @otter List every concern raised in this meeting, who raised it, and whether it was resolved. Add the timestamp for each one.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Turn it into minutes
paragraphs.text: @otter Write structured meeting minutes for this conversation with these sections: attendees, topics discussed, decisions, next steps.
On the free plan you get 3 Otter Chat questions per conversation and 20 a month, so make each one count. Ask for everything you need in one prompt instead of three small ones.
Otter says chat answers may sometimes be wrong or outdated, so check anything important against the transcript before you send it on.
Otter AI free plan limits

According to Otter's pricing page, the Basic plan includes 300 minutes of meeting and recording transcription per user per month, a 30 minute maximum per conversation, 3 imported files for the lifetime of the account, 20 Otter AI Chat questions a month with 3 per conversation, one meeting at a time, 5 custom vocabulary terms, and access to only your 25 most recent conversations.

Pro costs $16.99 per user per month billed monthly, or $8.33 per month billed yearly. It raises the limits to 1,200 minutes a month, 90 minutes per conversation, 10 imports a month and 50 chat questions a month, with unlimited conversation history. Business is $30 per user per month billed monthly, or $19.99 billed yearly, with unlimited meeting transcription and 4 hours per conversation. The pricing page also shows promotional prices for first-time subscribers.

The 30 minute cap is the limit most people hit first. A one hour team call on the free plan will not be transcribed in full, and the 25 conversation history means older notes drop out of reach unless you export them. For occasional short calls Basic works. For daily meetings, it is a trial rather than a tool.
Save and share your notes

paragraphs.title: Share a conversation
paragraphs.text: Open the conversation and click Share. Add email addresses and choose collaborator or viewer access, or copy a link.

paragraphs.title: Export a transcript
paragraphs.text: In My Conversations, open the menu on a conversation and choose Export. Pick a file format and whether to show speaker names, then export.
On the free plan, export anything you want to keep. Only the 25 most recent conversations stay available.

Otter also connects to other apps, including Slack, Google Docs, Notion, Asana, Jira, Salesforce and HubSpot, according to its homepage. It lists an MCP server that lets ChatGPT, Claude and other AI chat tools reach your meeting notes.
